subject: math
title: Likelihood: Impossible, Unlikely, Likely or Certain
seo_title: Grade 2 Likelihood Worksheets: Impossible, Unlikely, Likely, Certain (Free Math, Answer Key, BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Likelihood of familiar life events, using comparative language
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on likelihood: describe familiar events in BC as impossible, unlikely, likely or certain, use bags and spinners, compare events as more, less or equally likely, and make predictions from a few trials. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the BC curriculum.
key_big: Impossible: never. Unlikely: probably not. Likely: probably. Certain: for sure.
key_sub: Likely is not certain: if it might not happen, say likely. To compare two events, count each colour: more, less or equally likely.
body_html:
Four likelihood words

Likelihood tells how sure we are that something will happen. Use these words, from never to for sure:

  • Impossible: it can never happen.
  • Unlikely: it can happen, but probably will not.
  • Likely: it will probably happen, but not for sure.
  • Certain: it will happen for sure.
WordExample in BC
impossibleA ferry drives on the highway.
unlikelyYou see an orca from the ferry.
likelyIt rains in Vancouver on a November day.
certainToday is Monday, so tomorrow is Tuesday.

Bags and spinners

Look at what is in the bag. All red: red is certain. Most red: red is likely. Only a few red: red is unlikely. No red: red is impossible.

Example

Which word fits picking red? Which word fits picking blue?

Most counters are red, so red is likely. There is 1 blue, so red is not certain. Blue can happen, but probably not.

Answer: red is likely, blue is unlikely

More likely, less likely, equally likely

To compare two events, count how many of each. More counters means more likely. Fewer counters means less likely. The same number means equally likely. On a spinner, look at how big each part is.

Example

Compare landing on red with landing on blue.

Red has 2 sections. Blue has 2 sections. They are the same size.

Answer: equally likely

Predictions from a few trials

Try it a few times and look at the results. What comes up most often is likely to come up again. A few tries cannot show that something is impossible or certain.

Example

What is the best prediction for Hana’s next pick?

Red came up 8 times and blue 2 times. Red is likely. Blue came up too, so red is not certain.

Answer: Red is likely.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying certain when it is only likelyCertain means for sure, every time. If it might not happen, say likely
Saying impossible when it is only unlikelyIf it can happen even once, it is unlikely, not impossible
Not counting how many of eachCount each colour. More counters means more likely
Counting sections, not their sizeLook at how much of the spinner each colour covers
Choosing your favourite colourYour favourite colour does not change the chance
Thinking a coin is “due” for tailsHeads and tails are equally likely on every toss

faq.q: What do Grade 2 students learn about likelihood in BC math?
faq.a: In the BC curriculum (Data and probability), Grade 2 students describe the likelihood of familiar life events with words like impossible, unlikely, likely and certain. They also compare two events as more likely, less likely or equally likely.

faq.q: What is the difference between likely and certain?
faq.a: Likely means it will probably happen, but it might not, like rain on a November day in Vancouver. Certain means it will happen for sure, like Tuesday coming after Monday.

faq.q: What is the difference between unlikely and impossible?
faq.a: Unlikely means it can happen, but probably will not, like seeing an orca from a ferry. Impossible means it can never happen, like a ferry driving on the highway.

faq.q: How can I practise likelihood with my child at home?
faq.a: Put coloured blocks or socks in a bag and ask, “Which colour is more likely?” before picking. Talk about everyday events too, such as rain at recess or a snow day, using impossible, unlikely, likely and certain.

sets.title: Everyday events in BC: impossible, unlikely, likely or certain?

items.q: A sunny July day in Kelowna. July in Kelowna is hot and dry. Which word fits “It rains today”?
items.e: Rain on a hot, dry July day is not likely, but it can happen. So it is unlikely. It is not impossible: Kelowna does get some rain in summer.

items.q: A hot summer day at a lake in the Okanagan. Which is impossible?
items.e: Water does not freeze on a hot summer day. It can never happen, so it is impossible.

items.q: A hot summer day at the lake. Which is likely?
c: An orca swims in the lake.
items.e: On a hot day, many kids swim. That will probably happen, so it is likely. Orcas live in the ocean, not in lakes.

items.q: It is midnight in Kamloops. Which is certain?
items.e: At midnight the sky is always dark. That is certain. An owl or rain might happen, but not for sure.

items.q: Today is Monday. Which is certain?
items.e: Tuesday always comes after Monday, so it is certain. A sunny day is only likely or unlikely.

items.q: Today is Monday. Which word fits “Tomorrow is Saturday”?
items.e: The day after Monday is always Tuesday. Tomorrow can never be Saturday, so it is impossible.

items.q: Chloe is 7 today. Which is certain?
items.e: Every year you get 1 year older. 7 + 1 = 8, so it is certain. You cannot get younger.

items.q: Lucas lets go of an egg. Which word fits “The egg falls down”?
items.e: When you let go of something, it always falls down. It is not just likely. It is certain.

items.q: Leah leaves a popsicle in the hot sun for an hour. Which word fits “It melts”?
items.e: The hot sun always melts a popsicle. It will happen for sure, so it is certain, not just likely.

items.q: Harjot’s team plays a hockey game. Which is impossible?
c: The game ends in a tie.
items.e: Only one team can win a game. Both teams winning can never happen, so it is impossible.

items.q: It is a school day in Surrey. Which is likely?
c: You read a book at school.
There is a fire drill today.
items.e: Students read on most school days, so it is likely. A fire drill happens only a few times a year, so it is unlikely.

items.q: It is a school day. Which is unlikely?
c: The school turns into a cake.
A deer walks into your class.
items.e: A deer in class could happen, but it almost never does. So it is unlikely. A school turning into a cake can never happen: that is impossible, not unlikely.

items.q: It is a snowy winter day at Whistler. Which is likely?
items.e: Many people ski at Whistler on a snowy winter day, so it is likely. Swimming in an icy lake is unlikely.

items.q: A snowy day in Prince George. Which is impossible?
items.e: A snowman cannot talk. That can never happen, so it is impossible. The other things might happen.

items.q: It is November in Vancouver. It rains on many days. Owen says rain tomorrow is certain. Which word is better?
items.e: It rains on many November days in Vancouver, so rain is likely. But some days are dry. It is not for sure, so it is not certain.

items.q: Wei rides a ferry to Vancouver Island. Which is unlikely?
c: The ferry flies in the sky.
items.e: Orcas live near Vancouver Island, but you do not see one on most trips. So it is unlikely. Seeing the ocean is certain, and a flying ferry is impossible.

items.q: Wei rides a ferry. Which is impossible?
c: The ferry drives on the highway.
items.e: A ferry is a boat. It can never drive on a highway, so it is impossible. Seeing an orca is unlikely, but it can happen.

items.q: Which event is certain?
items.e: Every week has 7 days, so it is certain. A week with 9 days is impossible.

items.q: Ava takes the SkyTrain every day. She says, “The train will be on time tomorrow. It is certain.” Which word is better?
items.e: The SkyTrain is on time most days, so it is likely. Sometimes it is late, so it is not certain.

items.q: It is December in Prince George. Which is likely?
c: You swim in an outdoor lake.
It is a hot beach day.
items.e: Prince George is cold and snowy in December, so snow this week is likely. December has 31 days, so 40 days is impossible.

sets.title: Bags and spinners: which word fits?

items.q: You pick one counter without looking. Which word fits picking red?
items.e: Every counter is red. You will pick red for sure, so it is certain.

items.q: Which word fits picking blue?
items.e: There is only 1 blue counter and 5 red. Blue can happen, but probably not. So it is unlikely. Only 1 does not make it impossible.

items.q: Which word fits picking red?
items.e: Most counters are red, so red is likely. There is 1 blue counter, so red is not certain.

items.q: Which word fits picking red?
items.e: There are no red counters in the bag. You can never pick red, so it is impossible.

items.q: Which word fits landing on blue?
items.e: Every section is blue. The arrow must land on blue, so it is certain.

items.q: Which word fits landing on red?
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are red, so red is likely. There is a blue section too, so red is not certain.

items.q: Which word fits landing on blue?
items.e: Only 1 of the 4 equal sections is blue. Blue can happen, but probably not. So it is unlikely.

items.q: Which word fits landing on purple?
items.e: There is no purple section. The arrow can never land on purple, so it is impossible.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: There is only 1 green counter and 7 yellow. Green can happen, but probably not. So green is unlikely.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 6 of the 8 counters are blue, so blue is likely. There are red counters too, so blue is not certain.

items.q: On which spinner is landing on red certain?
items.e: Certain means it must happen. Only Spinner C is all red. On A, red is likely, but not certain, because there is a blue section.

items.q: From which bag is picking blue unlikely?
items.e: Bag B has only 1 blue counter and 5 red. Blue can happen, but probably not. In Bag D, blue is impossible, not unlikely.

items.q: On which spinner is red likely, but not certain?
items.e: Spinner D has 3 red sections and 1 blue. Red is likely, but blue can happen too. On A, red is certain. On B, red is unlikely.

items.q: From which bag is picking yellow impossible?
items.e: Bag A has no yellow counters, so yellow is impossible. Bag B has only 1 yellow counter, so yellow is unlikely there, not impossible.

items.q: Mei’s bag has 4 red counters and 2 blue counters. Red is likely. She wants picking red to be certain. What should she do?
items.e: Certain means every counter must be red. If the 2 blue counters come out, only red is left. Adding red counters makes red more likely, but not certain.

items.q: Arjun’s bag has 1 blue counter and 5 red counters. Blue is unlikely. He wants picking blue to be impossible. What should he do?
items.e: Impossible means it can never happen. With no blue counter left, blue can never be picked. More red counters make blue less likely, but still not impossible.

items.q: Simran rolls a number cube. Which word fits rolling a 7?
items.e: The cube has the numbers 1 to 6. There is no 7, so rolling a 7 is impossible.

items.q: Simran rolls a number cube. Which word fits rolling a 6?
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 faces shows a 6. A 6 can happen, but probably not. So it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Kai grabs one mitt from the box in the dark. Which word fits getting a blue mitt?
items.e: 4 of the 5 mitts are blue, so blue is likely. There is 1 red mitt, so blue is not certain.

items.q: A bag has 10 counters. Picking red is certain. How many red counters are in the bag?
items.e: Certain means every counter is red: all 10. With 9 red and 1 other counter, red is only likely.

sets.title: Compare two events: more, less or equally likely

items.q: Compare picking red with picking blue. Picking red is …
items.e: There are 6 red counters and only 2 blue. More counters means more likely.

items.q: Compare picking yellow with picking green. Picking yellow is …
items.e: There is only 1 yellow counter and 7 green. Fewer counters means less likely. It is not impossible: there is 1 yellow.

items.q: Compare landing on red with landing on blue. Landing on red is …
items.e: There are 2 red and 2 blue sections, all the same size. Red and blue are equally likely.

items.q: Kai says blue is more likely, because blue has 2 sections. Which is more likely, red or blue?
items.e: Do not just count sections. Look at their size. The red section is half of the spinner. The 2 blue sections are small. So red is more likely.

items.q: Zara says yellow is more likely, because yellow is her favourite colour. Which colour is more likely?
items.e: Your favourite colour does not change the chance. There are 7 green and 2 yellow counters, so green is more likely.

items.q: Which two colours are equally likely?
items.e: Count each colour: red 3, blue 3, yellow 2. Red and blue have the same number, so they are equally likely.

items.q: Put the colours in order from most likely to least likely.
items.e: Count each colour: yellow 5, red 2, green 1. The most counters is most likely: yellow, red, green.

items.q: From which bag is picking red most likely?
items.e: Each bag has 6 counters. Bag C has the most red counters (5), so red is most likely there.

items.q: On which spinner is blue less likely than red?
items.e: On Spinner C, only 1 of the 4 sections is blue and 3 are red. So blue is less likely than red there. On B, they are equally likely.

items.q: Liam puts 6 more green counters into the bag. Which colour is now more likely?
items.e: Green: 2 + 6 = 8 counters. Red: 6 counters. 8 is more than 6, so green is now more likely.

items.q: How many red counters must Nadia add to make red and blue equally likely?
items.e: Equally likely means the same number of each. Blue has 5. Red has 2. 5 − 2 = 3, so add 3 red counters.

items.q: It is November in Vancouver. Which is more likely tomorrow?
items.e: Vancouver gets a lot of rain in November and not much snow. So a rainy day is more likely. A hot beach day in November is very unlikely.

items.q: Which is more likely?
items.e: Whistler is in the mountains, and January is winter, so snow is very likely. Snow in Vancouver in July almost never happens.

items.q: It is a school day. Which is least likely?
c: A bald eagle flies into class.
items.e: Reading, lunch and recess happen on most school days. An eagle in class almost never happens, so it is least likely.

items.q: Ethan’s class has 15 girls and 12 boys. The teacher picks one name from a toque. Which is more likely?
items.e: There are 15 girls and 12 boys. 15 is more than 12, so a girl’s name is more likely. It is not certain, because there are boys’ names too.

items.q: A prize box has 20 prizes: 14 pencils, 5 stickers and 1 toy car. Olivia picks one without looking. Which is she least likely to get?
items.e: There is only 1 toy car, so it is least likely. There are 14 pencils, so a pencil is most likely.

items.q: A box has 9 grape popsicles and 3 cherry popsicles. Owen takes one without looking. Which is he more likely to get?
items.e: There are 9 grape and 3 cherry popsicles. 9 is more than 3, so grape is more likely. There is no orange, so orange is impossible.

items.q: Mateo picked red last time. He put it back. He says red is more likely now. Which is right?
c: Red and blue are equally likely.
items.e: Mateo put the counter back, so there are still 4 red and 4 blue counters. Red and blue are equally likely.

items.q: Noah wants red to be more likely than blue. Which spinner should he use?
items.e: Spinner D has 3 red sections and 1 blue section. Red is more likely there. On C, red and blue are equally likely.

items.q: Bag A has 3 red and 1 blue counter. Bag B has 4 red and 6 blue counters. In which bag is red more likely than blue?
items.e: Compare red with blue in each bag. Bag A: 3 red, 1 blue, so red is more likely. Bag B has more red counters, but even more blue: 4 red, 6 blue.

items.q: Hana picks a counter from a bag and puts it back. She does this 10 times. Which colour did she get more often?
items.e: Count each colour: red 8 times, blue 2 times. 8 is more than 2, so red came up more often.

items.q: Hana picks a counter from a bag and puts it back. She does this 10 times. How many times did she get blue?
items.e: Count the B circles: picks 3 and 8. That is 2 times. 8 is the number of reds.

items.q: Hana picks a counter from a bag and puts it back. She does this 10 times. Which bag did she most likely use?
items.e: Red came up much more often, so the bag likely has more red counters. It cannot be 10 red and 0 blue: then blue would be impossible, but she picked blue.

items.q: Hana picks a counter from a bag and puts it back. She does this 10 times. What is the best prediction for her next pick?
items.e: Red came up 8 of 10 times, so red is likely. Blue came up 2 times, so blue is not impossible, and red is not certain.

items.q: Owen’s spinner has 4 equal sections. Which spinner did he most likely use?
items.e: Red came up 9 times and yellow 3 times. Red probably covers more of the spinner. With 4 red sections, yellow would be impossible.

items.q: How many times did Owen spin altogether?
items.e: Add the tallies: red 5 + 4 = 9, yellow 3. 9 + 3 = 12.

items.q: What is the best prediction for Owen’s next spin?
items.e: Red came up most of the time, so red is likely. Yellow came up 3 times, so it is not impossible.

items.q: Arjun tosses a loonie 4 times. He gets heads every time. What about the next toss?
c: Heads and tails are equally likely.
items.e: A coin does not remember what happened before. Heads and tails are still equally likely.

items.q: Kai spins 5 times. He never gets blue. Is landing on blue impossible?
items.e: The spinner has a blue section, so blue can happen. 1 of 4 sections is blue, so it is unlikely. A few spins cannot show that it is impossible.

items.q: Lucas spins 10 times. Which result would be most surprising?
items.e: Half the spinner is red and half is blue, so you expect about 5 of each. Red every single time can happen, but it is very unlikely.

items.q: Ryan spins 8 times. Which prediction is best?
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are blue, so blue should come up much more often than red. Blue 8, red 0 is not a good guess, because red can happen.

items.q: Sofia picks a counter and puts it back. She does this 10 times. Which prediction is best?
items.e: There are 9 green and 1 yellow counter, so green is much more likely. Yellow can happen, so green every time is not certain.

items.q: Jasleen picks from a bag 6 times and puts the counter back each time. She gets blue every time. What is the best thing to say about the bag?
c: It has only blue for sure.
items.e: Blue every time tells us blue is likely. But 6 picks cannot show that every counter is blue. There might be another colour she did not pick yet.

items.q: Ava picks from a bag of green and purple counters. She puts each one back. Which word best fits picking purple next?
items.e: Purple came up only 3 times out of 10. It can happen, so it is not impossible. But it is less likely than green, so unlikely fits best.

items.q: Liam’s class spins a spinner 50 times. They get blue 38 times and yellow 12 times. What is the best prediction for the next spin?
items.e: Blue came up much more often, so blue probably covers more of the spinner. Blue is more likely, but not certain: yellow came up 12 times.

items.q: Owen rolls a number cube 12 times. He gets a 6 three times. How many times did he not get a 6?
items.e: Not a 6 means all the other rolls: 12 − 3 = 9.

items.q: Chloe spins 10 times. She gets red 5 times, blue 3 times and yellow the rest of the time. How many times did she get yellow?
items.e: Step 1: red and blue: 5 + 3 = 8. Step 2: 10 − 8 = 2 times yellow.

items.q: A bag has 1 red and 1 blue counter. Mei picks a counter and puts it back, 20 times. Which result is the best prediction?
items.e: Red and blue are equally likely, so about half of the 20 picks should be red: about 10. The other half, about 10, should be blue.

items.q: Noah tosses a toonie 6 times. He gets tails 4 times. Which is true about the next toss?
c: Heads and tails are equally likely.
items.e: A toonie has 2 sides, and each side has the same chance every time. A few tosses do not change that.

items.q: Hana got red 8 times out of 10. She says, “Red is certain next time.” Which word is better?
items.e: Red came up most of the time, so red is likely. Blue came up too, so red is not certain.

sets.title: Word problems: likelihood in BC life

items.q: At the school fun fair, there are 100 raffle tickets. Ava buys 1 ticket. Ethan buys 10 tickets. Who is more likely to win?
items.e: Ethan has 10 tickets and Ava has 1. More tickets means more likely to win. Ethan is not sure to win: there are 100 tickets.

items.q: A box has 20 granola bars: 15 chocolate chip and 5 oatmeal. Leah takes one without looking. Which is true?
items.e: Only 5 of the 20 bars are oatmeal. Leah might get one, but probably not. So oatmeal is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Each of the 24 students in Sofia’s class puts their name in a toque. The teacher picks one name. Which is certain?
c: The name is a student in the class.
items.e: Every name in the toque belongs to a student in the class, so that is certain. The teacher did not put in her name, so that is impossible.

items.q: Zara gets a point when the spinner lands on red. Lucas gets a point when it lands on blue. Each spinner has 4 equal sections. Which spinner is fair?
items.e: A game is fair when both players are equally likely to win. 2 red and 2 blue equal sections make red and blue equally likely.

items.q: Kai wins a prize if he picks red. Bag A has 3 red and 5 blue counters. Bag B has 5 red and 3 blue counters. Which bag should he choose?
items.e: Both bags have 8 counters. Bag B has 5 red and Bag A has only 3 red. Red is more likely in Bag B.

items.q: Rain is likely on the day of the class picnic in Stanley Park. What is a good plan?
c: Bring nothing, because rain is impossible.
items.e: Likely means it will probably rain, but not for sure. So keep the picnic, and bring rain jackets.

items.q: On the ferry, Wei looks for orcas. Seeing an orca is unlikely. Which is true?
c: He will see one for sure.
items.e: Unlikely means it can happen, but probably will not. So he might see one. Unlikely is not the same as impossible.

items.q: Lucas has 8 white socks and 2 black socks in a drawer. He grabs one sock in the dark. Which word fits getting a white sock?
items.e: 8 of the 10 socks are white, so white is likely. There are 2 black socks, so white is not certain.

items.q: Ryan has 30 stickers in a bag: 25 orca stickers and 5 eagle stickers. He picks one without looking. Which is true?
items.e: 25 of the 30 stickers are orcas, so an orca is likely. There are 5 eagles, so an orca is not certain and an eagle is not impossible.

items.q: A bag has 20 counters. 6 of them are red. How many counters are not red?
items.e: Not red means all the other counters: 20 − 6 = 14.

items.q: Arjun puts 10 blue counters in a bag. He wants red and blue to be equally likely. How many red counters should he add?
items.e: Equally likely means the same number of each colour. Blue has 10, so add 10 red.

items.q: A bag has 3 red and 3 blue counters. Nadia adds 6 more red counters. Which is true now?
c: Red and blue are equally likely.
items.e: Red: 3 + 6 = 9 counters. Blue: 3 counters. 9 is more than 3, so red is more likely. There is still blue, so red is not certain.

items.q: Mr. Kim’s class spins to pick a recess game. Which word fits playing tag?
items.e: Only 1 of the 4 equal sections is tag. Tag can happen, but probably not. So it is unlikely.

items.q: On the day of the Terry Fox Run, rain is unlikely. What does unlikely mean?
c: It might rain, but probably not.
items.e: Unlikely means it can happen, but it probably will not. It is not the same as impossible.

items.q: The weather report says rain in Victoria is likely tomorrow. Jasleen says, “So it will rain for sure.” Is she right?
items.e: Likely means it will probably rain. It might stay dry. Only certain means for sure.

items.q: A jar has 40 green marbles and 10 yellow marbles. Ji-woo picks one without looking. Which is more likely?
items.e: There are 40 green and 10 yellow marbles. 40 is more than 10, so green is more likely. There are no blue marbles, so blue is impossible.

items.q: Emma’s class tosses a loonie 30 times. They get heads 14 times. How many times did they get tails?
items.e: A loonie lands on heads or tails. Tails is all the other tosses: 30 − 14 = 16.

items.q: Zara wins if she rolls 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5. Harjot wins if he rolls a 6. Is the game fair?
c: No. Zara will win for sure.
No. Harjot is more likely to win.
No. Zara is more likely to win.
items.e: Zara wins on 5 faces. Harjot wins on only 1 face. They are not equally likely to win, so it is not fair. Zara is not sure to win: a 6 can happen.

items.q: A bag has 50 counters. Picking red is impossible. How many red counters are in the bag?
items.e: Impossible means it can never happen. So there are no red counters: 0. With 1 red, red is unlikely.

items.q: Owen picks a name from a toque with 30 names. His own name is on 1 paper. Which word fits picking his own name?
items.e: His name is only 1 of 30, so it can happen, but probably not. It is unlikely, not impossible.
